clue.text: Variety act by clever ape is most welcome

indicators.note: variety implies a mixed assortment, so the following words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A music-hall turn starring a clever ape is welcomed with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' looks like the music-hall setting but tells you to rearrange ACT BY CLEVER APE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is extremely acceptable is warmly received, hence most welcome.

clue.text: Descriptive of language foreign to Minorca…

indicators.note: foreign suggests something made strange or altered, so the island's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on a language not spoken on the Balearic island of Minorca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign to' rearranges MINORCA; the ellipsis links to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Romanic describes the Romance languages descended from Latin.

clue.text: … as well as Laos, strangely

indicators.note: strangely says the country's letters are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the language theme, Laos is listed alongside Minorca.
explanation.definitionFit: Also is an adverb meaning in addition, a synonym for as well as.

clue.text: Garment causing little Charles to change colour

parts.note: Chas is the familiar short form of the name Charles

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of the colour word to be altered into a new order

parts.note: blue is a colour

explanation.surface: An item of clothing makes young Charlie turn a different hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges BLUE (the colour) into UBLE, placed after CHAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is the sleeveless outer vestment worn by a priest at Mass.

clue.text: Suffer in an expensive way

parts.note: a phrase meaning to be punished for something, read literally as handing over money for a purchase

explanation.surface: Paying a heavy price for one's mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffer the consequences of something is to pay a price, while buying costs money.

clue.text: Sudden departure of a gruff one-time personality

parts.note: abrupt means curt or gruff in manner
ex means former or one-time
it means personal magnetism or appeal

explanation.surface: A brusque former celebrity storms off without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt exit is a hasty, unexpected leaving.

clue.text: Reason for not being able to see the wood for the trees, maybe

definitions.text: Reason for not being able to see the wood for the trees, maybe

parts.words: Reason for not being able to see the wood for the trees, maybe
parts.note: the idiom about missing the big picture is read literally, as greenery blocking one's view of the timber

explanation.surface: Explaining why someone misses the overall picture by fixating on details.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense foliage on trees can literally obscure the trunks behind.

clue.text: Short-lived perhaps, but I'm fast

parts.note: fast colours are permanent, ones that will not run

explanation.surface: Something boasts of lasting, though it is probably fleeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' means permanent here, as in a fast dye, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Impermanent things do not endure, so they are brief and transient.

clue.text: No catch in a bad year for the agent

indicators.note: in places the fielding failure inside the scrambled period of twelve months
bad suggests something spoiled, so the year's letters are jumbled

parts.note: to miss is to fail to catch

explanation.surface: A secret agent drops the ball during a disappointing twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges YEAR to EARY, and 'in' puts MISS inside after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a representative sent on a mission, an envoy or agent.

clue.text: Area worse for drink protected by Royal Marines

indicators.note: protected by means surrounded by the military abbreviation on both sides
worse for drink suggests something knocked about, so the beer's letters are scrambled

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A drunken neighbourhood kept safe by a marine patrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worse for' rearranges ALE to EAL, and 'protected by' puts it inside RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or field, an area of activity or rule.

clue.text: Trendy appreciation one gets no thanks for

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
gratitude is thankful appreciation

explanation.surface: A modish thankfulness that earns no reward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unthankful is what someone shows when no thanks are given in return.

clue.text: A trinity of trinities

parts.note: three groups of three each, read as a sum

explanation.surface: A religious triad multiplied by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Three threes make a number that is the square of three.

clue.text: Doesn't figure in the first three?

definitions.text: Doesn't figure in the first three?

parts.words: Doesn't figure in the first three?
parts.note: an unplaced runner in a race fails to finish in the top three positions

explanation.surface: A competitor fails to make the podium.
explanation.definitionFit: Unplaced in a race means literally lacking a placing, and generally being unsuitable.

clue.text: Potted version of parts one said

definitions.text: Potted version of parts one said

indicators.note: a potted version is a condensed rearrangement, here of the letters

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A summary of some speech fragments a person uttered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potted version of' rearranges PARTS, I and SAID; the whole clue also describes the classic houseplant in its pot.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is the archetypal potted parlour plant.

clue.text: Mineral giving the sailor a shake-up?

parts.note: to rock is to shake
salt is slang for an old sailor

explanation.surface: Some mineral substance gives a seaman a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a verb and object: shake the seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salt is halite, the naturally occurring crystalline mineral form of sodium chloride.

clue.text: Compensate old counsel backing me

parts.note: rede is an archaic word for advice or counsel

indicators.note: backing means the following word is turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: A former adviser supports me to make up for a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ME into EM after REDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem a fault is to make amends or compensate for it.

clue.text: Left suffering and become depressed

parts.note: anguish is severe suffering

explanation.surface: Abandoned and in pain, someone sinks into gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to pine or lose spirit, growing weak and dejected.

clue.text: Plan to move in less than a set-end

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Plan to move in less than a set-end', looks garbled by OCR: no reading of 'less than a set-end' gives the letters of TACTIC, and a search found no source.
annotationWithheld.clue: Plan to move in less than a set-end

clue.text: About to go a large number stuck together

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
to leave is to go away
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Approximately set to depart, a crowd clung together.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleave has two opposite senses; here it means adhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaved in the sense of adhered means clung fast or joined closely.

clue.text: Reputed charmer with stray animals at Tynemouth

parts.note: the mouth, or start, of the Tyne is its first letter, T

indicators.note: stray suggests wandering off, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A snake-charmer type with wandering beasts at a Northumberland port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stray' rearranges ANIMALS plus T, the opening of 'Tyne'; Tynemouth is a town at the River Tyne's mouth in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object believed to have magic powers, a lucky charm.

clue.text: Drink Swallow first

indicators.note: first means the bird comes before the single letter in the answer

parts.note: the martin is a bird of the swallow family

explanation.surface: A tippler gulps a drink down before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' is the bird, not gulping; 'first' puts it ahead of I.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth.

clue.text: Great finish for one of the car drivers

definitions.meaning: a large conclusion or final stretch
a connecting-rod bearing at the crankshaft that helps drive a car engine

explanation.surface: A grand ending for a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a large tail end, and in engineering the crankshaft end of a connecting rod.

clue.text: Specified number of rulers unwelcomed as early colonists

parts.note: the is the definite article, pointing to a specified thing
VI is the Roman numeral six
kings are rulers

explanation.surface: A certain group of monarchs received coldly by settlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse raiders settled parts of Britain but were hardly welcome there.

clue.text: A single Sussex flower

parts.note: in cricket a single is one run

explanation.surface: One lone bloom growing in a southern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows, a river; Sussex is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arun is a river flowing through West Sussex to the sea at Littlehampton.

clue.text: Taught orally albeit wrong

indicators.note: orally means the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: taught is the past tense of teach

explanation.surface: Instructed by spoken word, but incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A tort is a civil wrong for which a court can award damages.

clue.text: Sod ironed out on the golf course

definitions.text: Sod ironed out on the golf course

parts.words: Sod ironed out on the golf course
parts.note: a piece of turf knocked out by a golfer's iron club, not smoothed flat

explanation.surface: A clump of turf struck loose during a round.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's iron shot often gouges out a chunk of turf from the fairway.

clue.text: Copies I'd made of a series of events

indicators.note: made here means formed into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Duplicates someone produced of a sequence of happenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodic means occurring in separate instalments or incidents.

clue.text: His famous son was a white man, nevertheless

definitions.text: His famous son was a white man, nevertheless

parts.words: His famous son was a white man, nevertheless
parts.note: the king's eldest son was nicknamed the Black Prince, though he was of course white

explanation.surface: A father noting that his celebrated boy was not literally black.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Prince, the famous warrior son of a fourteenth-century English king, got his nickname perhaps from his armour.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourteenth-century English monarch's eldest son was Edward of Woodstock, the Black Prince.
